Third glossary term: embeddings

One new definition on schedule: the glossary runbook ships its third term in backlog order, with the page, the backlog flip, the social pack, and this log entry landing together.

m
Machine Made WorldsSep 09, 2026 · 2 min read

In this article

Follow the journal ↗

The weekday glossary runbook continues with its third term: an explainer on embeddings, the number lists that place similar meanings close together for search by meaning. The new page renders at the embeddings explainer, the backlog marks the term shipped while keeping its order and aliases, and this log entry ships beside it in the same change.

Motivation

The journal points readers at fresh model behavior every day, yet newcomers keep tripping over the vocabulary underneath it. A weekday glossary turns each such question into a page that teaches and interlinks, and the runbook ships one term per run in backlog order. The third slot belongs to the vectors behind search by meaning, so readers meeting similarity search for the first time have somewhere to land.

What changed

A new explainer now renders at the embeddings explainer: a one-line definition, a short section on the shared-space mapping, and a closing line on when builders reach for it. It is filed under topic essays as kind Glossary with the featured flag untouched, and the builder appends the related-terms block automatically. The backlog entry keeps order three with both aliases and flips to shipped, and a beside-each-article pack carries the short social copy with the canonical link.

How it was done

After the hosting preflight and a fresh branch from the main line, development flipped the backlog flag, drafted the term page from the runbook pattern, and added the pack plus this log entry in the same change. No template, style, or builder changes were needed: the existing article page supplies the eyebrow, lead, and related grid, while the shipped aliases start linking older posts automatically. The social copy was counted by hand against its limits before saving.

Verification evidence

The site build exits success, the full suite is green, and the presence gate prints success with this entry covering the change. The built glossary page shows the definition, the explainer section, and the auto-inserted related block, while the sitemap and feed include the new address. A scan of the diff finds no secrets, and security plus quality reviews attach to the exact pushed head after this pull request opens.
